fix_subject: fix(queue): end queued input only on a recorded cause (#200433)
cause_quote: #198245 made a policy evaluation failure non-terminal by wrapping the owners' revocation in `if (!isOperatorAuthorityUnavailable(error)) { revoked = true; ... }` and documenting that it 'refuses this operation without revoking its source', but left the followup runner, drain and mailbox readers ending custody on any `assertCurrent()` throw.
user_saw: With an access-policy plugin, a message queued during a temporary policy outage was dropped (shown as withheld) and never answered after the policy recovered.
summary: Authority owners now abort their signal on a revocation found by assertCurrent, and queue/mailbox/steer readers end an input's custody only on recorded abort, retirement, cancellation or consumption rather than on any failed assertCurrent check.
reasoning: The readers that drop queued input on any assertCurrent throw predate the outage notion (the followup runner already consumed input on any throw before #200213, which only made the drop visible as 'withheld'); dropping became wrong when #198245 introduced the GatewayOperatorAccessUnavailableError contract that a policy outage is non-terminal, without updating the queued-input readers (#198729 then patched only some steer/mailbox paths). So the outage-preservation behavior never worked for queued followups; medium because the defect is an incomplete cutover of the introducing change rather than a single bad line.
